reason: I'd probably download it and start the free trial since there's no auto-charge, but I've tried enough sleep apps that I don't expect to end up paying. I already play free sleep sounds on YouTube, and money is tight, so a phone guessing when I fell asleep isn't enough for me to pay every month.
objection: Can a phone sitting next to my bed really tell when I fell asleep? If the numbers are a guess, the '14-day comparison' is just marketing with a chart.
would_change_my_mind: If the day-14 report showed I fell asleep at least 10 minutes faster on the SLEEP:ON nights, and that matched how I actually felt in the mornings, I'd pay for the 4,900 won monthly plan.
